identity: Zeiss Axioskop marking visible in photo254; head variant, complete objective inventory and socket count partly provisional
geometry_basis: Photo254/255/256/257/258/261/262: photographed housings and controls; reference5 corrects the stage aperture to a front-to-back obround and replaces the solid support slab with an open two-arm fork. Dimensions remain estimates; sample/objective/grip datums unchanged.
reference5_construction: Top aperture44x92 mm and lower opening46x94 mm are photographic estimates. Native contacts use open strips and tangent boxes with less than0.12 mm circular-edge undercoverage, not convex hulls spanning the light path.
control_geometry_correction: XY gear housing slimmed; both XY grip links moved+15 mm X/-25 mm Z to clear focus wheel across Y travel. Clearance1 additionally lowers the gearbox roof2 mm and recesses its two fasteners so the moving X deck clears them across full travel; contact envelope moves with it. Couplings and sample/objective sites unchanged. Opposite focus grip contact added on same existing focus-wheel joint.
alignment6_correction: Fixed holder plate now rests on the deck and supports the existing glass underside without penetration. Rounded concave holder and retaining-arm footprints use compound convex-prism contacts, with pivot, thumb lever and clamp screw contacts; no convex hull spans the specimen opening. The thumb lever uses its evaluated beveled mesh and each objective front shoulder follows its actual distal taper, with separate aperture and reveal contacts. Small holder-plate bevels remain within conservative contact envelopes.
optical_contact_model: Dedicated objective/work-surface contact bits preserve robot contact and exclude mated bearings. Objective front shoulders and existing forward glass surfaces have explicit contacts. Retract the stage before changing objective; high focus commands can legitimately meet the specimen. Focus and XY shaft ranges match the existing linear stops through their unchanged pitches.

imaging.light_path_calibration: Three-position beam splitter is an explicit legacy Zeiss phototube approximation, not identification of the fitted lab head.

assumptions: Five sockets and objective order are modeling choices. Scale, focus pitch and loads estimated from photographs.

contact_mechanics.coupling_relation: output = ratio * input; input/output/ratio metadata remains unchanged
contact_mechanics.friction_units: N m for hinge joints, N for slide joints
contact_mechanics.calibration: Numerical stabilization with estimated friction; no measured torque, compliance, backlash, or mass calibration is claimed.
contact_mechanics.scope: Preserves geometry, masses, inertias, existing gravity compensation, and active fixture forces. Adds no holding actuators or position overwrites.
limitations: Flexible hoses and fibers are visual surfaces without cable contact or strain physics.
